title: Stalling prefetch circuit and rescue playbook
body:
Summary:

Over a 6-hour window on 2024-11-05 we observed repeated host-side request stalls that manifested as 99th-percentile tail latency spikes for text-generation routes. The immediate trigger was an extended prefetch coordinator pause that starved the continuous-batching queue: jobs were accepted into the scheduler but could not progress because the KV index rebuild worker was holding an exclusive compaction lock while prefetch backoff timers mis-calculated remaining work. Symptoms looked like a deadlock from the request path perspective (inflight requests queued, no forward progress) but memory and CPU were stable on hosts until a second stage of prefetch retries amplified memory use and caused host-level OOMs on a subset of hosts.

Why this doc exists:
- Capture what we saw, quick triage steps, and a short rescue playbook for oncall.
- Record hypotheses and short/long-term mitigations for SRE + runtime eng.
- Collect concrete metrics/queries and owners for follow-ups.

Immediate impact observed:
- 99th latency for /v1/generate routes increased from ~250ms baseline to 4–8s for affected tenants.
- Per-host inflight queue depth increased to >500 in staging-like hosts and >1200 on prod smaller instance types.
- ~8 hosts entered OOM kill over a 2-hour subwindow during prefetch retry amplification.
- Customer-facing errors: 502/504 spikes for latency-sensitive routes, no widespread data loss.

Quick triage checklist (first 15m):
1) Identify affected hosts and tenants
   - PromQL: sum by(host) (inflight_requests_total{job="serving-runtime"})
   - PromQL: topk(50, inflight_queue_depth{route=~"/v1/generate.*"})
2) Check prefetch coordinator and KV rebuild status
   - kubectl -n runtime logs <prefetch-pod> -c prefetch-coordinator --since=30m
   - grep for "prefetch: backoff" / "kv-rebuild: compaction lock"
3) Look for recent dynconfig or deploys that touch prefetch/backoff logic
   - git log --oneline --follow services/prefetch/* | head -n 20
   - Check changelog in PagerDuty alert body (deploy tags attached)
4) If inflight queue growth + no forward progress: enable emergency bypass
   - Dynconfig: prefetch.enabled=false for the affected shard (temporary)
   - If dynconfig unavailable, apply feature-flag toggle via admin API: POST /admin/feature-flags {"prefetch": false}
5) If host memory trending up rapidly: cordon host and migrate traffic
   - kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>

Observed root-candidate causes (priority-ordered hypotheses):
A) Prefetch backoff mis-estimation: we under-calculated remaining prefetch work leading to a long sleep period where the coordinator held a compaction/exclusive lock, preventing the KV index rebuild from yielding. This created queue starvation and then retry amplification.
B) Compaction lock priority inversion: a low-priority background compaction took a lock while higher-priority prefetch tasks waited for an event; scheduling jitter caused prefetch timeouts and redundant retries.
C) Batching queue head-of-line starvation: continuous-batching rosters expected a steady arrival rate; pauses from the prefetch coordinator created sudden bursts that confused the scheduler heuristics and allowed some tenants to monopolize microbatch slots.
D) Edge-case race on prefetch coordinator restart: if coordinator restarts mid-rebuild, it can leave ephemeral lease entries that the rebuild scanner treats as live, leading to repeated rebuild attempts and unbounded retry loops.

Investigation artifacts / PromQL primitives to run during triage:
- inflight queue: sum by(host) (inflight_queue_depth{job="serving-runtime"})
- prefetch lock holds: increase(prefetch_lock_hold_seconds_sum[5m]) / increase(prefetch_lock_hold_seconds_count[5m])
- kv rebuild attempts: rate(kv_rebuild_attempts_total[1m])
- batch occupancy: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(batch_fill_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- per-tenant throttles: sum by(tenant) (throttle_events_total{job="serving-runtime"})

Rescue playbook (fast, safe steps):
1) Short-term toggles (0–30 minutes)
   - Disable prefetch for impacted shard(s) to stop coordinator holding compaction locks: dynconfig prefetch.enabled=false.
   - Reduce kv_rebuild_concurrency to 1 on affected hosts to avoid compaction overload: dynconfig kv.rebuild.concurrency=1.
   - Enable per-tenant request throttling at the edge to reduce burst pressure: set route-level RPS caps for high-traffic tenants.
   - Temporarily route traffic away from smallest instance types that have less headroom (use routing weight dynconfig).
2) Medium-term rollback / configuration (30–180 minutes)
   - If emergency toggles restore latency, perform a controlled rollback of the last deploy that touched prefetch or kv compaction code.
   - Gradually restore prefetch with conservative timeouts and monitoring on mediantoken path.
3) Host-level actions (if OOMs observed)
   - Mark host as drained and reprovision a replacement; gather heap profiles and /proc snapshots before reboot.
   - If many hosts impacted, expand capacity via autoscale for Dedicated pools and enable fallback to hosted model variants.

Runbook snippets to include in main playbook (post-incident):
- How to safely flip prefetch dynconfig per-shard.
- How to read lock-hold histograms and interpret compaction skew.
- SRE command snippets to force graceful leader election for coordinator: kubectl exec -n runtime <coord-pod> -- /usr/local/bin/coordctl force-leader-stepdown

Telemetry to capture for postmortem (what to attach):
- Timeline of inflight queue depth and prefetch lock hold durations at 10s resolution.
- Per-host memory RSS and oom_kill events with kernel messages.
- Correlation of deploy IDs / PR numbers to first occurrence of elevated kv_rebuild_attempts.
- Heap/alloc profiles from affected host(s) during retry amplification period.

Immediate mitigations owner list (who does what):
- Maya Patel (SRE): flip prefetch.enabled false for affected shard, coordinate with runtime infra to drain hosts.
- Jonah Kim (runtime eng): triage compaction lock code path, add defensive yields in compaction path.
- Priya Desai (SRE): run telemetry queries, collect logs and prepare the incident timeline.
- Luca Moretti (platform): issue dynconfig patch and cut safe rollback if deploy implicated.

Action items for engineering (post-incident):
1) Add a bounded-yield to compaction path so it never holds exclusive lock > X seconds (owner: Jonah, ETA: 2 weeks).
2) Make prefetch backoff estimator conservative by default and add a max-sleep upper bound (owner: runtime-eng, ETA: 3 weeks).
3) Add a coordinator restart reconciliation that clears stale lease entries within 15s (owner: runtime-eng, ETA: 2 weeks).
4) Implement per-tenant microbatch fairness token bucket to prevent single tenant from monopolizing restored batch slots (owner: platform-team, ETA: 6 weeks).
5) Instrument a "prefetch_hold_time" SLI and wire alerting at 95th > 3s.

Notes and open questions:
- We still need to confirm whether the compaction lock was held because of a bug or because rebuild saw more live entries than expected after a prior GC. Priya to correlate GC window with rebuild size.
- Is the retry amplification pattern visible across all model types (embeddings, chat, legacy generation)? Early signs point primarily at long-context generation routes.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Collect inflight tasks and thread stacks (from runtime admin pod):
  curl -sS http://localhost:9000/admin/inflight | jq '.' > /tmp/inflight-$(date +%s).json
- Snapshot prefetch coordinator state:
  kubectl -n runtime exec <prefetch-pod> -- cat /var/run/prefetch/state.json > /tmp/prefetch-state.json
- Quick Prometheus snapshot URL to include in time-series attachments:
  https://prometheus.internal/graph?g0.expr=sum%20by(host)(inflight_queue_depth)%20&g0.range_input=1h

Quick retrospective takeaways:
- Avoid long exclusive locks in critical read-path interactions (compaction + prefetch).
- Defensive limits on retry/backoff logic are cheaper than trying to recover from amplification.
- Short toggles (disable-prefetch) are effective stopgaps but we should automate safe toggles with runbook play buttons in Console.

Status: Draft runbook and incident notes. This file will be converted into a cleaned runbook page and linked from the SRE incident postmortem once we validate root causes and assign owners for code changes.
